reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because the supplied frames and narration present a television segment examining Bitcoin, its mining process, price history, and individual miners rather than directing viewers to make a payment, surrender credentials, or join a deceptive earning scheme. The narration includes historical and interview-based claims about Bitcoin profits, but the communicative format is reporting and financial commentary, with no explicit creator call to action or participation pathway.

citations.quote: At the moment of the interview, a bitcoin was worth $ 812 which means that Vlad Mandiuc made $ 116 in 2 days
This is the evolution of price, per hour, per day and so on, per minute

opening.argument: Judge, the earning claim is tied to a concrete paid activity. The segment says a miner invested €1,700 in a Bitcoin-related application and reports a profit one month later. It then projects thousands of dollars by month’s end from mining without further work. That pairing of an upfront investment with apparently passive mining income does more than explain how Bitcoin works; it presents participation as a way to earn.

citations.quote: in December 2013 invests 1700€ in the strange application made by the guy that says it's going after bitcoin. A month later it did, and now there is a good profit.
at the end of the month, the miner will have 3-4,000 USD, without doing anything.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The interview and price chart cited by the defense establish a reporting format, but format does not settle the effect of the message. The €1,700 expenditure is followed by a claimed profit, and the narration projects $3,000–$4,000 by month’s end without work. There is no explicit enrollment instruction; the concern is that the segment makes paying to mine look like a readily profitable choice.

citations.quote: in December 2013 invests 1700€ in the strange application made by the guy that says it's going after bitcoin. A month later it did, and now there is a good profit.
at the end of the month, the miner will have 3-4,000 USD, without doing anything.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The €1,700 figure describes one interview subject’s past investment, not a purchase offered to viewers. The projected monthly amount is expressly conditional on the currency continuing at the same pace. Neither passage identifies a mining package, seller, payment route, or invitation to participate. The segment’s discussion of price movements supports reading these claims as financial reporting, even if its projections are optimistic.

citations.quote: in December 2013 invests 1700€ in the strange application made by the guy that says it's going after bitcoin.
And if the currency will run at the same pace, at the end of the month, the miner will have 3-4,000 USD, without doing anything.
This is the evolution of price, per hour, per day and so on, per minute

opening.argument: Judge, consider the combined impression of the income claims. Mining is described as producing a substantial asset with “zero effort”; the narration says the device enriches its owner while working by itself. Later, it gives a two-day dollar figure, projects thousands more within a month without doing anything, and describes a Bitcoin address receiving mined money every day. Those are unusually easy, recurring-reward claims attached to operating a mining setup, not merely an abstract discussion of a currency.

citations.quote: how you can make a fabulous asset with zero effort.
But that enriches you every minute, just letting this strange device work by itself.
Vlad Mandiuc made $ 116 in 2 days And if the currency will run at the same pace, at the end of the month, the miner will have 3-4,000 USD, without doing anything.
the username is your bitcoin address, where they will put money that was mined by you inside everyone else everyday

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that a price chart and an interview appear, but those elements do not neutralize the repeated easy-income language. The narration moves from an interviewee’s two-day earnings to a month-end projection and says mining requires no further action. The issue is the impression created by that progression, even without an explicit payment demand.

citations.quote: Vlad Mandiuc made $ 116 in 2 days And if the currency will run at the same pace, at the end of the month, the miner will have 3-4,000 USD, without doing anything.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These excerpts use promotional-sounding language, but they do not tell viewers to complete a task, submit a Bitcoin address, or claim a reward. The daily-address description concerns money mined by the interview subject, and the larger monthly figure depends on an explicit assumption about the currency’s pace. The segment also discusses increasing mining difficulty, context that the easy-reward reading leaves out.

opening.argument: Judge, a news-style presentation can still promote a purchase. Here, the narration introduces an acquaintance who bought Bitcoin, follows with a story of what the sale enabled, and later emphasizes dramatic past price gains alongside the possibility of much larger future value. That selection of examples makes buying Bitcoin appear to be the route to a life-changing return. The broadcast framing gives those anecdotes the appearance of reported evidence, while the forward-looking appreciation claim supplies the incentive to participate.

citations.quote: In the summer I met my client who bought 20 bitcoins for $100 each, A friend of mine bought a few coins for her and she sold them in a 4-month sale. She bought a fiat, took a vacation
the value of a bitcoin could be tens or hundreds of times bigger
In 2012, bitcoin price was $3. From 2012 until 2013, at the beginning, the price has reached $12! So it has gone up 4 times in a year...

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense points to an interview and price history as signs of commentary. Those same devices can lend credibility to a buying narrative: the segment recounts a purchaser’s gains and says Bitcoin’s value could grow tens or hundreds of times. The absence of a transaction link limits the claim, but it does not erase the promotional force of the examples chosen.

citations.quote: A friend of mine bought a few coins for her and she sold them in a 4-month sale. She bought a fiat, took a vacation
the value of a bitcoin could be tens or hundreds of times bigger

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A purchaser’s past experience and speculation that value “could” rise do not amount to an offer to sell tokens or instructions to buy them. The segment also describes Bitcoin’s mining mechanics and changing difficulty. Its interview and price discussion can be enthusiastic or imprecise without establishing a deceptive purchase scheme directed at viewers.
